trajectory_summary: This is a short, purely logistical call: an existing solar owner calling back about a battery-only need, and the rep spending almost the entire call negotiating a workable time slot around her job schedule. There is no qualification, no bill discussion, and no interest-reason exploration because the customer's need was already narrowly defined before the rep picked up.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear from metadata, but the observed outcome is a booked appointment for a specific day and time (Saturday the 25th at 11 AM) — this should be tagged 'booked' with the caveat that no standard verify/qualify content was run, since the customer was routed straight to scheduling for a narrow battery-only ask.

observed_outcome.quote: K. Sounds good. K. We'll do 11AM next Saturday. That's gonna be the twenty fifth.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Saturday the 25th) and time (11 AM) were explicitly agreed upon, meeting the criteria for a booked outcome. Channel (phone vs. in-person) was never specified in the call.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: No bill amount or usage figure was ever discussed — the call was purely about rescheduling for a battery-only need, and the rep never asked about a utility bill.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The customer volunteered her reason for interest (battery backup for her existing solar system) without being asked, but the rep never probed further into WHY she wants the battery (outage history, cost, etc.) or referenced it again before booking.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: orphaned-flow qualifying skipped on existing-solar-owner call
primary_coaching_focus.quote: All I needed was, like, batteries.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer disclosed she already owns a solar system and only wants a battery — this is squarely the orphaned_flow scenario, and none of its three qualifying questions (ownership type, original installer, system working) were asked before scheduling. If her existing system is leased/PPA or broken, this appointment is a wasted closer slot.

key_moments.quote: No. The thing is the person said that, you guys have a Delta solar panel for me to take a look at. But I was saying I already have solar panel. All I needed was, like, batteries.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is an orphaned-flow scenario (existing solar owner) combined with a battery-only ask — outside the standard new-install script. The rep does not run any of the orphaned_flow qualifying questions (owns vs. leases the existing system, which company installed it, is it working).

key_moments.quote: let me look at yeah. It says it's just for a battery. That's just a generic text that goes out.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer just handed the rep a clean anchor (battery-only need on an existing solar system) and the rep filed it as an administrative note rather than asking why she wants a battery now (power outages? new usage? distrust of grid?).

key_moments.quote: Would you be able to talk about that battery tomorrow?
key_moments.stewart_read: This begins a five-round scheduling negotiation with no structural anchor (no stated call length, no 'is that fair' handshake) until the very end. The rep is proposing times without framing what the appointment actually covers.

key_moments.quote: I'll shoot you a text so you have it in writing. Okay?
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep does promise a text follow-up, which is good procedure, but the button-up otherwise skips the one-hour block statement, the no-driving/computer instruction, and any recap of what the appointment will cover.
